summary: Per-tenant adaptive migration to new quant/batching profile causing intermittent 5xxs — request for guided shadow rollback
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported intermittent 5xx errors and high tail latency after we enabled a per-tenant adaptive optimizer profile (adaptive batching + prefix-KV caching + new 8-bit quant profile) during a staged migration. Impact: production traffic from BrightClinic experienced 10-15% request errors and elevated p99 latency between 11:30 and 13:00 UTC.

Impact:
- ~12% of requests returned 5xx for a subset of tenant requests (multi-turn chat flows).
- Elevated p99 latency from 480ms to 1.8s for affected endpoints.
- Customer revenue-impacting: clinical decision assistant queries timed out for end users.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dc-eu-east-1a (customer-dedicated-045) routed through us-east control plane for this migration.
- Serving runtime v2.6.3, optimizer-service v1.9.0 (feature flag: adaptive-per-tenant-v2).
- Config: per-tenant profile applied via optimizer API, enabled KV-prefetch: true, batching: adaptive (max_batch=128, latency_target_ms=40), quant_profile: profile-v8-qat.

Steps to reproduce (customer flow):
1) Tenant sends a multi-turn chat request with average prompt length ~850 tokens and generate length ~400 tokens.
2) Request routed to dedicated pool and enters adaptive batching path.
3) When batches hit hybrid slow path (mixture of long sequences and short), some workers reported OOM-evictions or high GC pauses in runtime, leading to connection resets and 5xx.

Observed behavior:
- Connection resets and 502/504 spikes in CloudLB and gateway logs.
- Worker logs show transient KV cache mismatch warnings (eviction race) and quant-decode retries.
- Autoscaler did not spin up new GPUs during the window due to burst capacity gating.

Expected behavior:
- Adaptive profile should smooth batching without causing OOM or decode failures and fallback safely to a lower-cost path without user-visible 5xx.

Logs/Attachments:
- Attached API request IDs: [rcpt-20241105-1123-az, rcpt-20241105-1127-qd] (in ticket comments).
- Link to metrics snapshot: https://rwd-console/metrics/brightclinic/2024-11-05/11-30-13-00

Customer request:
- Immediate guidance to safely revert per-tenant profile (shadow rollback) and a checklist for migration to prevent reoccurrence.
comments: 2024-11-05 12:05 - Support (Maya Chen): Acknowledged. Opening investigation and coordinating with SRE to capture worker logs and autoscaler trace. Asking customer to provide a couple of failing request IDs and whether they can route a small repro traffic to a staging pool.

2024-11-05 12:18 - Customer (BrightClinic - Priya Rao): Provided request IDs rcpt-20241105-1123-az and rcpt-20241105-1127-qd. We can divert a replay of 1% of traffic to staging if needed. Impacting urgent clinical flows — please expedite.

2024-11-05 13:02 - SRE (Daniel Park): Observed repeated 'kv-prefetch eviction race' messages and 'quant-decode retry' errors in worker logs for that tenant's worker set. Autoscaler policy blocked burst due to a configured budget cap. Opening hotfix plan with runtime team.

2024-11-05 14:30 - Runtime Eng (Nora Singh): Hypothesis: new quant profile increases transient memory pressure with large multi-turn KV caches, causing evictions and a cascade of decode retries. Suggest shadow-rollback path: toggle tenant feature-flag to legacy optimizer profile-v7, disable kv-prefetch for tenant, lower adaptive max_batch to 64 while observing metrics for 30m.

2024-11-05 15:10 - Support (Maya Chen): Performed staged rollback for tenant: 1) applied legacy profile-v7 snapshot 2) set kv-prefetch=false for tenant 3) adjusted max_batch to 64. Monitoring now. Customer confirmed improvement in a small replay run.
2024-11-05 15:45 - Customer (Priya Rao): Replay confirmed — errors dropped to <1% and p99 latency returned to ~420ms. Thanks; want post-mortem and migration checklist.

2024-11-07 09:12 - Support (Maya Chen): Ticket being closed after providing post-rollback runbook and follow-up items. Recommending gated re-rollout with staged canary, memory headroom checks, and temporary per-tenant circuit breaker for quant profile changes.
investigation_notes: Captured worker logs from dedicated pool and correlated with customer request IDs — saw 'kv-cache-evict-race' followed by quant-decoder fallback on same worker threads.
Heap and GPU memory profiles indicate spikes coinciding with long sequence requests, pushing memory over configured headroom when combined with new quant code-path allocations.
Autoscaler policy prevented quick burst due to per-tenant budget - this prolonged worker saturation window and increased error exposure.

Hypothesis: quant-profile-v8 introduces temporary additional decode buffers and metadata, incompatible with high KV cache residency for long-turn conversations; adaptive batching's max_batch=128 increased variance causing straggler pressure.
Regression check: no similar errors in other tenants using same profile but with shorter typical sequence lengths; suggests workload-specific interaction.
Action taken: executed per-tenant shadow rollback (legacy profile snapshot restore) and disabled kv-prefetch to reduce memory churn. Verified through replay and metrics that errors remediated.

Follow-up recommended: add preflight memory simulation for per-tenant optimizer changes, add per-tenant circuit breaker for quant/decode failure spikes, and improve autoscaler burst thresholds tied to optimizer transitions.
resolution:
Performed safe per-tenant shadow rollback to legacy optimizer profile (profile-v7 snapshot). Steps executed: 1) locked tenant config to prevent auto-retries of migration job, 2) applied snapshot restore of profile-v7 via optimizer API, 3) disabled kv-prefetch on tenant, 4) lowered adaptive max_batch to 64, 5) monitored for 45 minutes and ran 1% traffic replay. Observed errors fall from ~12% to <1% and p99 latency returned to baseline.

Post-rollback follow-ups delivered to customer and internal teams:
- Runbook: 'per-tenant optimizer migration preflight' with memory headroom checklist and simulated replay (confluence link provided).
- Work item opened with runtime team to add graceful fallback in quant decode path and to reduce transient buffer allocations (see PR infra/optimizer-config#4212).
- Autoscaler policy change proposal to allow a limited burst for first 10 minutes after optimizer profile toggles.

Customer accepted rollback and requested staged re-rollout only after preflight checks. Ticket resolved and turned into operative guidance for future per-tenant migrations.
postmortem_tasks: Create per-tenant optimizer preflight script and CI job (owner: Runtime Eng)
Implement quant-decode graceful-fallback to drop to lower-memory path before returning 5xx (owner: Runtime Eng)
Adjust autoscaler burst gating to allow temporary capacity for optimizer transitions (owner: SRE)
Document runbook and publish to customer-facing migration guide (owner: Developer DX)
